relations: Leaves swaying gently across the sun modulate glare exposure, partly hiding then diffusing the white center.
Changing backlit leaf angles cause individual leaves to flash brighter or darken into silhouettes.
The faint lens-flare disc persists and drifts as sun-leaf geometry shifts with the swaying foliage.
The leaf border framing the sky stays consistent while central clusters and branches shift position.
caption: The video captures a low-angle view looking up through green oak leaves that frame the edges against a pale blue sky. The sun shines toward the camera from near the center, creating a strong white glare and a faint circular lens-flare disc. Throughout, the leaves sway gently and continuously, so the central cluster and surrounding branches shift slightly in position and orientation. This movement changes glare exposure, making it partly hidden then more diffused as leaves drift across it. Individual leaves flash brighter or darken as their backlit angles change, while some stay translucent green and others form darker silhouettes. The leaf border remains consistent, so the main motion comes from swaying foliage and shifting glare. The faint lens flare persists and drifts with the changing sun-leaf geometry.
